title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography, created by manipulating video to show people's faces in sexual situations without consent, appeared on a platform receiving millions of monthly visitors. The victims were prominent Dutch women including entertainers, politicians, athletes, and members of the royal family. The system had no detection or verification mechanism to prevent non-consensual intimate imagery from being hosted.

The failure occurred at the platform level. The site operated a business model rewarding anonymous users for uploading content, with payment based on views, and no apparent moderation to identify or remove manipulated sexual material. Catching this would have required either automated detection of deepfake pornography before upload, human review of flagged content, or verification that people depicted had consented to being shown in sexual scenarios.

It is not established how the deepfake videos were created or what specific AI tools or services were used to generate them, only that manipulated videos appeared on the hosting platform and that such content is illegal under revenge porn laws.

summary:
Several prominent Dutch women are considering legal action after their faces appeared in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The platform contains fake videos featuring Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file police reports. Managers and representatives confirmed that some victims have already filed reports or are exploring legal options.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. Users who upload such material are advised to remain anonymous and receive payment based on video views. Legal experts recommend that victims file police reports, which may allow prosecutors to shut down the website. Other options include starting a class action lawsuit, filing complaints with the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, TV presenter Welmoed Sijtsma became a victim and made a documentary about her case. A 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a conditional sentence of 180 hours in November for creating fake videos of her.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
